title: Self-Service Analytics
objectives: Explain the key ideas behind Self-Service Analytics.

definition: Self-Service Analytics is a core concept in Data Analytics. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Self-Service Analytics is
theory.body: Self-Service Analytics describes the methods and patterns used within Data Analytics to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Self-Service Analytics is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Self-Service Analytics matters
theory.body: Without Self-Service Analytics, systems built with Data Analytics are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Self-Service Analytics works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Self-Service Analytics follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Self-Service Analytics.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Self-Service Analytics
theory.body: Self-Service Analytics offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
